1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs

Let me screenshot current state.
Image read successfully

4. Progress bar at very bottom partially cut? It's at panel bottom edge y=661 with panel ending 681 - fine but squashed against edge.
5. Empty space in mine bigger now.

Let me improve mine scene: the miner should be center-bottom, prompting above miner? Better: place prompt above the action row at bottom maybe 130px, and center miner higher (bottom 27%). Actually prompt currently at bottom 112; action row bottom 48 height 48 → action row spans 48-96 from bottom. prompt at 112 → just above. Miner at bottom 19% (87px) spans up 124 → overlaps prompt. Raise miner to bottom 28%? Panel 460, prompt at ~112-128 from bottom. Miner bottom 87 + height 124 = 211 from bottom, crossing prompt. Put miner bottom at 24% = 110, still overlaps. Better place prompt to left side? Or place prompt above the mine at like top 44% centered? Actually simplest: move prompt near the ore vein (top ~58%)? Hmm.

Alternative design: put the mine prompt right above the action row and the miner on the right side of center so prompt central-left doesn't overlap. But the miner should be central.

Better: move prompt to just under mine header, e.g. top 110px, centered — clean. "CLICK TO SWING · +1 ORE". And keep miner center bottom. Also add a small floating hint near the ore vein. Let me set .mine-prompt to top:98px; bottom:auto.

Also increase contrast of mine scene floor. Also the pickaxe looks like floating stick; maybe fine at small scale.

Also progress bar: add padding-bottom and make progress wrap have a dark gradient background so text readable. Actually text "NEXT DEPTH 1/30" is on cave background, low contrast. Add background gradient at bottom.

Let me also make the mine panel cave scene have a floor line and some small rocks for more polish. Could add scattered pebbles via CSS. And fix ore vein appearance: shape with gold gradient looks okay-ish; make it more rocklike with darker border.

Also top-right reset button small arrow looks odd; make it a gear/reset icon pill with label? It's fine but maybe style consistent: .reset-btn circle. Add CSS.

Also the day pill says "SHIFT 01 · ON THE CLOCK". Fine.

Gameplay test: click mining, sell, buy. Need to quickly test via eval clicking button several times, sell, then buy pickaxe maybe. Also test idle auto after buying drill. Test depth advancement maybe set state via localStorage and reload? Could simulate by clicking many times using eval loop calling button clicks (DOM) quickly; but mine() adds and renders each time; 30 clicks should reach depth 2. Let's do 30 clicks and see depth. Actually there's toast spam; fine.

Also check save works. Let's evaluate localStorage.

Mobile responsive test at 390x844. Resize and screenshot.

Let me first adjust CSS/HTML for prompt and better scene.

Also "click to swing" prompt should mention "SPACE" on desktop? Already footer. Fine.

Improvements for idle incremental depth:
- Auto-mining buys drill and crew. Currently depth advances from idle ore, good.
- Ore values: iron/gold unlocked by depth. Good.
- Buying upgrades increases costs.
- Sell value multiplier.
- Offline earnings capped 8h.
- Reset button.
- No prestige. Idle incremental could use prestige, but not necessary? "complete, playable" — maybe add a Prestige/""New Vein" mechanism? Could enrich. The game as is: mine → sell → buy → deeper. There's an ending? Infinite. Maybe add milestone and deeper regions with better ore odds. That's enough. But an incremental game benefits from prestige. Could add "Retire & Reopen" prestige with permanent bonus tokens. Might be over-engineering but adds depth. Let's consider time. We have plenty.

Add a "Company legacy" prestige when depth 25: reset coins/upgrades/ore but keep permanent "Legacy tokens" giving +10% ore value and +1 starting pick power per token. But UI space? Could add small section in right column bottom, or a footer button "RETIRE (requires depth 25)". This adds meaningful long-term progression. Yet requirement is just playable idle incremental mining; current loop suffices. I'd rather polish polish UI and ensure mechanics.

However depth progression thresholds 30*d^1.28: depth 1→30, depth 2→67, 3→122, 4→176, 5→235, ... depth 10 → 30*19=570. With idle rates, reachable. Upgrades scale. Fine.

Water: showing coins as "⛃" glyph maybe renders as small. Fine.

- progress bar markers.

Miner: pickaxe arm looks like small stick; increase size, rotate. Fine.

Wait: mine-shade has z-index 1 and miner no z-index (auto) — miner is after shade in DOM so paints above? Elements with z-index 1 vs auto: shade z-index 1 creates stacking context above auto content, so miner would be behind shade gradient. Gradient is mostly semi-transparent; still dims miner. Set miner z-index:2 and mine-prompt z-index 4 already, controls z 3. Also floor z0, pebbles z1.

Set .miner{...;z-index:2}. Currently .miner has no z-index. Let's patch.

The main issue: svg is positioned with right:-22 bottom:26, width 86 → spans from miner right edge -22 to +64? So it covers the head region. Actually miner width 98, svg right -22 means right edge at 98+22=120; left at 34 → over body/head. Should be further right: right:-44px → left at 56, covering right half, head at top right of miner. Better.

Also head shape should be more like a pick: a horizontal-ish bar with downward-curving pointed ends, not a big arc. Perhaps use a simple double-headed pick:
<path d="M6 22 C 20 10, 34 8, 44 12 L 44 18 C 34 16, 24 20, 14 30 Z"/> (left head) and mirror right? Actually a pickaxe head is one piece: central eye at handle, two arms curving down at ends. Draw:
M4 26 C 16 10, 36 6, 48 10 L 44 18 C 34 15, 20 19, 12 30 Z for left half, and right half mirrored M44 10 C 56 6, 70 12, 80 26 L 72 30 C 64 20, 54 16, 44 18 Z. Combined with handle intersecting at x=44. This creates classic pick head with two pointed ends down. Use a single path:
"M3 28 C14 12 32 5 44 7 C56 5 72 12 81 28 L71 32 C63 21 54 16 44 15 C34 16 24 21 15 32 Z" — smooth. Ends at left (3,28) and right (81,28), bottom points. Hmm.

Classic pick: central hump, two tips pointing downward at ends:
M2 30 C 12 15, 30 7, 43 8 C 56 7, 73 15, 82 30 L 72 32 C 62 22, 54 18, 43 18 C 32 18, 23 22, 13 32 Z.
This yields crescent with downward tips. Fine—it looked like an umbrella because the head was too thin arc above; with side position it may be okay.

Also the handle bottom should not go below hand; with svg bottom 26, handle bottom y=92 → page foot; looks like it's planted on ground behind body? The screenshot shows handle crossing body and ending near bottom left of body → looks like a walking stick. We should shorten handle so it ends at the hand (y ~ 65) and put hand at that point.

Better construct svg where handle spans y=20..74, hand grips at y=68. Position svg so grip aligns with hand (~bottom 48 → within miner at y=98-48=50 from top? Actually miner coords bottom 48 = y=124-48-15=61 top of hand; hand center y=68). Hmm miner local: height 124, hand bottom 48 → top 61, center 68. Grip should be at local y=68. SVG height 96 positioned bottom 26 → svg top at 124-26-96=2; grip at svg y=? For grip local 68 → svg y = 68-2 = 66. So handle should end at svg y≈70. Good: rect y=18 height=52 (to 70). So .pickaxe height:80, width:96, bottom:46px, right:-38px. Then svg spans x from miner width? right -38 → right edge 136; left 40. Covers right half. Head center at 44 of 96 → local x=40+44=84, near right edge (98) and above right shoulder. Good, not above head.

Handle from x≈38..44, leaning? If rotate 20, top right. Head center at viewBox 44, handle top should meet at 44,10. Put rect x=40 y=14 width=6 height=58 rotate(18 43 43) → top around x=47, bottom x=37. Grip bottom at svg 70 → local x≈37+40=77, which is outside body (body right 71) but inside arm region. Hand at local x=~89? Hmm arm end near 465 page → local 89. Grip at 77-40? I'm confusing.

Pick svg left position = 98 - (-38) - 96 = 40 (local coords). Grip svg x ~38 → local x=78. Hand local x = 98-(-1)-15 = 84..99? .hand right:-1 width15 → left=84, right=99. So hand center 91.5. Grip at 78 → 13px gap left of hand. Adjust handle x or right offset. Set .pickaxe right:-28 → left=30, grip local 68? no grip x 38+30=68. Worse.

Alternative: align hand over grip by setting hand right to whatever. Simpler: set .hand at right:-8 (left 91?) no.

Let's not over-engineer. The previous CSS pickaxe looked like a hammer but positioned sanely; the SVG looks like an umbrella because too centered/overhead. Move it right and shorten handle + make head wider with pointed ends. We can eyeball.

Set .pickaxe{right:-46px;bottom:40px;width:96px;height:84px} with viewBox 0 0 96 84. Handle y=16..76 (visible 60). Head path around y=4..20. Then head local x center 44+ (98+46-96=48) = 92 → local position x=92, just right of head (head is x=27..74, center 50). So pick head to the right side of the miner, not above face. Good.
Grip bottom: svg bottom=40 → handle bottom local y=124-40=84? Wait svg top local =124-40-84=0. Handle bottom svg y=76 → local 76; hand center local 68. Close. Move bottom:32 → svg top=8, handle bottom local=84. Hmm.

Let's set svg bottom:24, height 84 → top=16. Handle bottom svg 76 → local 92 (below hand at 68), too low.

Set bottom:44, height 84 → top=-4, handle bottom local=72, hand center 68 → good. Svg extends above miner 4px, fine head at local ~2-20 (above helmet 25, okay). Pick head local x = left offset + 44. Left offset = 98 - (-46) - 96 = 48. So center x=92 → local 92, only 6px inside right edge, head extends 0..96 in svg → local x 48..144, way outside miner. So head is to the right, not over face. Good.

Handle grip local x ~ 48+38=86 → hand at 84..99, aligned! Great. So:
pickaxe right:-46 bottom:44 width:96 height:84.
Handle: rect x=38 y=12 width=6 height=64 rotate(20 41 44) → bottom around y=76, x~34 → local x=82. Good.
Head at top y=2..20 centered x=44.
Hand right:-1 bottom:48 → top 61 center 68, grip y local 72 → close.

But svg overflow visible; fine.

The head path:
M2 26 C14 10 32 3 45 5 C58 3 76 10 88 26 L78 30 C68 18 57 13 45 12 C33 13 22 18 12 30 Z
This is a crescent with tips down. It might still look like a crescent. Add an eye block at center: rect x=41 y=5 width=8 height=14 fill steel.

Actually classic pickaxe icon: handle vertical, head horizontal with two curved prongs pointing down. The above does that. With stroke.

Let's also raise head size maybe. Fine.

Big empty space at bottom of desktop. Could reduce to give more content or center. Options:
1. Add a "Mine log" panel or "stats" to right column. Adds content and interest. Could add a small panel "SHIFT NOTES" with tips and stats (ore per click, crit chance, sell multiplier). But content already shown. Or "Records" panel: deepest depth, best haul.

Setting .app min-height:100vh with flex? Could vertically center content if shorter: body display:flex align-items:center; .app width 100%. Add `body{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center}` and .app width:100%. But footer and padding? body currently min-height 100vh. This centers app vertically when short. At 900, top ~120 (content 660 → 120 margins). Looks more balanced. But on desktop wide, top bar no longer near top; is that good? Often game screens center. I think yes.

Alternatively add a fourth panel to right column that fills: "Fortunes" or "Deepest dig" with records. Actually a prestige/prestige-ish "Company ledger" with records could fill ~120px. Let's think about adding prestige to deepen gameplay. The user asked "idle incremental mining game" — a prestige layer is a hallmark. But complexity/time. We could add "Assay Office" that converts depth into permanent ore value? Hmm.

Potential additions:
- Achievements/records panel: "Deepest depth", "Best haul", "Total shifts". Low gameplay value.
- A second tab "MINE" with upgrades, or a "Boost" active ability (e.g., Frenzy) to make active play more engaging. Could add a timed "Dynamite" ability: every 60s, blast yields 30s of production. That's more complexity.

Given the game is playable and has progression, no need. But polish empty space by centering.

Let's add body flex. Ensure .app has width 100%. Currently max-width 1440 margin auto padding. Add width:100%.

On mobile, body min-height 100vh, flex center could cause content top cut if content taller? Flex with align-items:center on a container taller than viewport? body min-height 100vh with content taller will grow body; align center no issue. But safe area. Add `display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center`? .app only child plus toast/modal fixed. Use body{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center}. When content taller, body height auto and justify center irrelevant. Fine.

Wait body with min-height 100vh and flex column; .app width auto? set width:100%.

- The click button label "MINE ORE" and the mine prompt "CLICK TO SWING" could confuse: two click targets. But clicking the scene should also mine? Currently only button + space. For an idle game, clicking the cave should mine too. Add `minePanel` click handler, but avoid triggering when clicking buttons/tabs (they're inside panel only mine/sell). Add click listener on minePanel: if target closest button return; else mine(). Also change prompt "CLICK THE CAVE OR PRESS SPACE · +2 ORE". Mobile text may be too long. Keep "TAP THE CAVE · +2 ORE"? Use "CLICK / TAP TO SWING · +2 ORE". Good. Add pointerdown to allow touch.

Mining by tapping the big scene is satisfying. Implement:
$('minePanel').addEventListener('pointerdown', e => { if(e.target.closest('button')) return; mine(); });
But pointerdown on panel plus click on button: button is inside. prevent duplicate via closest.

Then click button triggers both click (onclick) and pointerdown (panel): pointerdown fires before click; closest('button') true for button so skipped; button onclick fires. Good.

Space listener active unless target button; fine.

Also add burst particles? Float text already. Could add rock chip particles for juice. Simple CSS particles via spans? Optional. Float text + miner swing sufficient.

- Depth progress bar color changes by region maybe; currently gold. Fine.
- Sell all button duplicated (sell button + sell entire cart). OK.

- Purchasing: disabled buttons show cost; when not enough muted. Good.
- There's no max levels.
- No sound. Adding WebAudio mining "clink" would enhance. Optional; could add subtle synth click on mine, coin sound on sell, upgrade chime. Games benefit. But audio autoplay restrictions: triggered by user gesture, fine. Add tiny WebAudio context lazily on first mine. Could be nice but risk. Let's consider: a short noise/oscillator "tink" at 400-800Hz with exponential decay; on crit higher. Sell = two-tone coin. Buy = rising. Add mute toggle? Without mute, might annoy; add sound toggle in top bar. That increases scope. Maybe skip audio; visual is enough.

- Add tooltips? no.

- Add offline gains correctly uses s.last but then save... fine. But initial load s.last from save; if offline, adds ore but also then render; yes. However beforeunload save updates last.

- Potential bug: after offline load, s.play not advanced by offline time; fine.

- Save load merges upgrades; if new upgrade keys added, defaults provide. Good.

This is a real bug: clicking "Erase save" → localStorage.removeItem then location.reload → beforeunload fires save() → writes current s back. So reset doesn't work. Need fix: set a flag `resetting=true` and save() skip if resetting; or clear then set s=fresh and save. Simplest: confirmReset: s=fresh(); active; save(); location.reload(). Actually just s=fresh() then localStorage set fresh state, reload; beforeunload saves fresh state. That works. Or set a `let wiping=false` and in save if(wiping)return. Implement wiping.

Let me fix that. Also test reset.

- Focus visible? Default outline may be removed? We didn't remove, fine.

Eh scaling maybe 720 height was actual viewport? innerHeight 900 now. Fine.

Empty area under mine panel (114px) is noticeable in screenshots: mine ends at 585 preview*? In crystal.jpg, mine panel bottom ~585/720, right col extends to 648. Yes there's blank below mine within left column? Actually screenshot left col: mine panel ends at 585, then footer at 648, while right col ends at 648. There's empty area below mine but it's page background, looks fine because footer. Hmm mine panel 460 and left col stretched to 687 leaves 114 blank below mine inside left col; but visually it's just background — same as right column ending. Not bad.

Add `.left-col .mine-panel{flex:1}` but careful min-height. Then mine panel height 574, scene taller, buttons still bottom. The miner bottom 26% moves up. Prompt at 104 top. Good.

Do it: `.left-col .mine-panel{flex:1}`. Then cave panel height ~574; controls remain bottom. The miner and cave look bigger. Good.

Hmm now bigger cave but the left col mine panel extends to 646 vs right 648. The cave now has huge empty middle with ore vein left and crystal right and miner center; composition okay. But the scene's bottom 150px is empty dark, with buttons. The mine prompt at 284; miner around 450-530; lots of gaps. Fine.

But the ore vein/crystal are positioned at 40%/31% so upper-middle; the scene's lower half is empty. With taller panel, the scene composition has too much empty bottom. Could reposition ore vein and crystal lower (top 45%/38%) and increase sizes; or use panel height not stretch (revert flex). The previous 460 looked more compact. The current 574 has a very large lower void (buttons overlay ~110). Hmm.

Maybe make mine panel not stretch and instead add another panel below it in left col to fill: e.g., a "Shift stats"/"Mining log" panel. That adds useful info and fills. But could look cluttered.

Alternatively adjust scene element vertical positions using percentages relative to full height; ore at 40% = 230, h 25% = 143, ends 373; crystal at 31% = 178, h 94; miner bottom 26% = 149, feet 425. Scene bottom 574. So lower 150 has miner and buttons. Fine actually. The screenshot shows lots of purple darkness right of miner below crystal, but a cave is dark. Could add some more rocks/pebbles to fill bottom right. Maybe add another ore chunk bottom for depth. 

But note the ore vein looks like a giant purple polygon floating with a dark rock outline. It reads as a purple gem deposit. Good.

The "NEXT DEPTH" progress bar at bottom y=655 and controls y=585. Fine.

Composition is acceptable but the big empty dark area between prompt (284) and miner head (434) is 150px. Could add hanging lamp light cone or a background mine cart. Adding a mine cart would be cool: a small wooden cart on the right bottom. Or a lantern hanging at top right. A lantern adds warmth and fills space. Let's consider adding a hanging lantern from the ceiling, top right, with a glowing cone. It would fill top-right empty space and look great. But effort with CSS. Could add simple lamp: a small div with radial glow and a chain. Positioned right 15%, top 0, chain height 60, lamp circle 14. Hmm.

Alternatively add a wooden "depth marker" sign. Not necessary.

The biggest polish issue is the right column and mine height mismatch? Now they match nicely.

Let's evaluate mobile after flex change. Also fresh state screenshot for first impression.

Concern: body centered with margin auto causes app height 866 and full page; on 1280x900 no scroll. On 1440? fine. On shorter laptop (1280x720), page taller than viewport → scroll; body flex center with overflow? body min-height 100vh; content 866 > 720, body grows to 866; flex centering no negative margin; top starts 0 (justify center can't center overflow? In flex, if content overflows, justify-content center may cause top clipping? Actually with overflow, centering can push content above the viewport top, a known issue: `justify-content:center` on a flex container whose content overflows may clip the top because free space is negative and it centers negative space. Yes! This is a real risk: with body min-height 100vh and content taller than viewport, align/justify center with negative free space puts equal negative offsets, clipping the top and making it unscrollable. Since body height grows? A flex container with min-height 100vh but auto height: its used height becomes max(content, 100vh) = content, so free space 0; no negative. Wait body min-height 100vh, height auto; if content 1200 > 900, body height becomes 1200 (auto), free space 0, so no clipping. Unless body height is fixed 100vh. It's min-height, so fine. Hmm but margin auto? The app has margin auto and content 1200, body 1200, no free space. Fine.

Mobile content taller → body grows → no clipping, scroll. Good.

One more issue: at 600px breakpoint we set .mine-panel min-height 435 and flex:1; in single column, left col height auto = content; mine flex:1 no free space. Good.

Let's screenshot mobile now (crystal state, but fine) with 390x844.

Visual problems on mobile:
1. The seal "CURRENT CLAIM · CRYSTAL HOLLOWS" wraps to 2 lines due to narrow width and depth badge; title below. It's okay but the eyebrow wraps awkwardly ("CRYSTAL / HOLLOWS"). Could shorten region name display or reduce font. Maybe set eyebrow white-space nowrap with overflow hidden; "CURRENT CLAIM · CRYSTAL HOLLOWS" at 8px might fit in ~280px. Currently width constrained by badge. Could make header flex with gap and allow eyebrow to nowrap + hide overflow. On 390, eyebrow 27 chars * ~5.5px = 148px, fits in 390-30-80 = 280. Why wrap? It shows "CURRENT CLAIM · CRYSTAL" then "HOLLOWS" — because the text plus badge. Hmm maybe letter-spacing .17em adds. 27 chars * (8*0.6+1.36) ≈ 166. Should fit. But `.eyebrow` width maybe 140 because flex item shrink? The badge takes ~90; remaining ~260. Hmm.

Actually on mobile .mine-header left 15 right 15 → width 360. Badge ~75. Left div width ~260. Eyebrow: 166 fits. But screenshot shows wrap after "CRYSTAL" at x~180, so container width ~150. Why? `.depth-badge` has flex? It's within flex; left div maybe shrinking due to long mine-title? Title "Crystal Hollows" 150. Hmm.

Maybe because .mine-header uses display:flex with align-items:flex-start and no gap; the left div's min-width auto may be 150? The eyebrow text 166 > that? It should expand. Could add `.mine-header>div:first-child{min-width:0}` and `.eyebrow{white-space:nowrap}`. On 390, the left div width 260 so nowrap fits. The wrap suggests available width 150; because the depth badge overlaps? no.

Wait the badge shows "DEPTH 26 m" wrapped to 2 lines ("DEPTH 26" / "m"), because width constrained! This indicates the flex container is distributing widths weirdly: both left and badge are shrinking below content due to flex-shrink:1. The badge text wraps. Need `flex-shrink:0` on badge and nowrap. Then left gets rest. Fix:
.depth-badge{flex:0 0 auto;white-space:nowrap}
.mine-header>div:first-child{min-width:0}
.eyebrow{white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}

This will fix both wrap issues.

2. The depth badge "DEPTH 26 m" wrapping currently makes header taller; fix.
3. The miner and ore vein larger due to scene? They look nice. But mine panel tall 435 and the composition is good. The bottom progress bar extends beyond? No, panel ends ~655, progress at 628. Good.
4. Buttons: "MINE ORE" wide (190px), "SELL ORE 2,597" 115px. Good touch targets.
5. "Pickaxe power 6 · 9% critical" right aligned below buttons. Good.
6. "NEXT DEPTH 838/1,942" and bar. Good.
7. The prompt pill text fits. Good.
8. Stats visible. Top bar: reset button. Good.
9. Workshop partially cut at fold; scroll. Fine. But on mobile, maybe the order should put ore cart + milestone before upgrades? Currently workshop first. The mine → workshop → cart → milestone. That's okay.

10. The vertical scrollbar appears; fine.

11. Footer way below.

We should ensure "tap the cave" works on mobile (pointerdown). Yes.

12. On mobile, the cave scene's ore vein is at top 37% of 435=161, height 126; screenshot shows it at 340-470 page. Fine.

13. Shop entries: buy buttons with price; good. Tap target 48px? Upgrade rows 66, buttons ~38 high. Fine; Apple recommends 44px; could bump buy button padding on mobile to 9px. Minor.

14. Reset button 40x40 maybe.

15. Topbar brand: "DEEP ROCK" looks good.

Fix header wrapping and maybe increase mobile shop button height. Also the mobile "SHIFT" is hidden; no session timer, acceptable.

Another thing: mobile viewport screenshot 390x844 shows content extends; maybe the game main action is all visible above the fold at 844 up to end of mine panel (655). Great.

Now fresh-state desktop screenshot. Need remove injected state (reset), then screenshot 1280x900. Also test crystal region done; iron region done. Deep region maybe quickly check color (should amber). Optional but cheap: inject depth 51 with save override. But then reset. Let's do deep screenshot quickly after fixing header.

Also check the game's accessibility contrast: muted text small but okay.

Fix header CSS.

Mobile looks nice. Issues:

1. Cave mineral shapes: The ore rock looks like a giant tan dodecahedron and the crystal a green gem floating. With the miner holding pickaxe, it's charming. But the scene's ore vein and crystal look like they're floating in air rather than embedded. The dark rock outline behind ore is visible, helps.

2. On mobile, the mine scene taller relative; prompt at ~283; miner head ~380. There's a large empty band between prompt and miner/ore (~60px). Fine.

3. Sell button "SELL ORE 6" fits. Ready highlight very subtle; border gold. Fine.

4. "Pickaxe power 2 · 3% critical" right aligned under buttons; fine.

5. The progress bar is nearly full but the fill is gold; good.

6. The "NEXT DEPTH" bar is at panel bottom, good.

7. The reset button top right (↻) small; fine but maybe add title.

8. On mobile, saved pill "GAME SAVED" visible while day pill hidden. Good.

9. The stats "Wallet 3" etc. Good.

10. Scroll: Workshop starts below; good.

11. Touch targets: Mine button 190x48. Sell 115x48. Great.

12. The ore cart card: "SELL ENTIRE CART 6" etc.

13. At 390, the mine panel bottom progress bar and text are within panel. Good.

One visual concern: "CLICK THE CAVE OR TAP TO SWING" is somewhat redundant ("click...or tap"). Could say "TAP THE CAVE TO SWING" on mobile via CSS content? Keep both is fine but slightly awkward. Could change to "MINE THE CAVE · TAP OR PRESS SPACE" but that's longer. Maybe "TAP / CLICK THE CAVE TO SWING". Hmm. "CLICK THE CAVE OR TAP TO SWING" implies click the cave OR tap anywhere. It's accurate: tapping the cave works. Fine.

14. The sparkle texture makes the cave feel textured. Good.

15. The mine ceiling dark band cuts through behind prompt? no.

Potential improvement: show "+1 ore" floating when clicking the mine button; it appears at 43%-61% left, top 46-61% — on mobile this appears near center below ore. Good.

One noticeable bug: The idle production means copper counts increment every second; screenshot shows lifetime 21 and copper 6, wallet 3. Good.

Test 320px width for stats overflow. Use resize 320x700, screenshot maybe. Check scrollWidth and any clipped. Also check the right column 2-col layout at 768. Let's do 320 and 768 checks quickly.

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('index.html');s=p.read_text()
start=s.index('@media(max-width:360px){')

block=s[start:end]

assert marker in s, 'marker not found'

p.write_text(s)

Now final test: reload, verify no JS errors, click mine, sell, maybe check save after 5s, reload persistence. Also perhaps test offline gains quickly by modifying last timestamp and reloading with no override? We can test:
- localStorage save has last; set last=Date.now()-60000 and rate>0? Fresh rate 0. Could buy drill? Not necessary.
- Offline code is straightforward.

Test persistence: mine, sell, buy pick, wait 6s, reload, check values preserved (but beforeunload saves anyway). Good.

Check the fix to header at 320 done.

Also verify CSS has no syntax errors due to inserted media. The page loads and screenshot fine.

Let's take final desktop screenshot fresh-ish. Reset via UI then maybe mine a bit for a lively screenshot. Also verify localStorage save after 5s.

Actually we should reset to fresh state at the very end so first-time players see 0. But browser state isn't shipped. Not relevant.

Let's run a final functional test sequence:
1. Reset.
2. Click mine 5 times (wallet?).
3. Sell (coins 5).
4. Wait 6s, check localStorage exists.
5. Reload, check coins 5, buy pick disabled? cost 12 >5. Set by clicking maybe.
